newsitem.title: USA: New York lawyer to represent accused bomber.
newsitem.headline: New York lawyer to represent accused bomber.

text.p: The alleged mastermind of the 1993 World Trade Centre bombing, Ramzi Ahmed Yousef, will be represented by court-appointed lawyer Roy Kulcsar in next year's trial, Kulcsar said on Thursday in U.S. District Court.
Yousef was one of the world's most wanted fugitives until he was arrested in February 1995 in Islamabad, Pakistan.

He and his co-defendant, Eyad Ismoil, a Jordanian, go on trial in late March or early April for their alleged roles in the trade centre explosion that killed six people, injured more than 1,000 and caused millions of dollars in damage.
Yousef was indicted in 1993 on charges of taking part in the bombing along with four others, who were convicted in 1994. Yousef left the United States on the day of the bombing, prosecutors said.
Ismoil is accused of driving the van that carried the 1,200 pound (544 kg) fertiliser bomb into the basement garage of the World Trade Centre complex.

Yousef remains in a federal prison in New York as he and two other defendants await sentencing after they were convicted in September of conspiring to bomb 12 airliners filled with Americans to punish the United States for its support of Israel. In that case, Yousef defended himself, although he has no formal legal training.
